title: Investigating the Impact of Learner Errors on Social Bias in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.29896v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing social bias benchmarks evaluate large language models mostly on fluent, well-formed English, reflecting native speaker usage and leaving non-native writers unrepresented. To address this gap, we investigate how grammatical errors by non-native writers affect social bias. We develop a controlled framework that injects common learner errors into prompts and apply it to three bias benchmarks covering stereotype alignment and demographic preference across gender, race, and religion. We find that grammatical errors increase bias, and the effect grows with the error rate. Among the four common error types we consider, preposition errors produce the largest and most consistent increase in stereotype alignment. Our analysis suggests that errors increase bias when they are more likely to interfere with comprehension. translated_title: 探究学习者错误对大型语言模型中社会偏见的影响
translated_abstract: 现有的社会偏见基准测试大多在流畅、规范的英语上评估大型语言模型，反映的是母语使用者的用法，而未将非母语写作者纳入考量。为填补这一空白，我们研究了非母语写作者的语法错误如何影响社会偏见。我们开发了一个受控框架，将常见的学习者错误注入提示中，并将其应用于三个偏见基准测试，涵盖性别、种族和宗教方面的刻板印象一致性以及人口群体偏好。我们发现，语法错误会加剧偏见，且这种影响随错误率的增加而增强。在我们考察的四种常见错误类型中，介词错误导致刻板印象一致性出现最大且最一致的增幅。我们的分析表明，当错误更可能干扰理解时，其加剧偏见的作用更强。最后，在含错误文本上进行微调可以减少语法错误造成的偏见增加。我们的发现表明，偏……
tldr: 该研究首次系统考察了非母语写作者的语法错误对大型语言模型社会偏见的影响，发现错误率越高偏见越强（其中介词错误影响最大），并通过在错误文本上微调有效缓解了这一问题。
en_tdlr: This study systematically investigates how grammatical errors made by non-native writers amplify social bias in large language models, showing that bias grows with error rate (with preposition errors having the largest effect) and that fine-tuning on erroneous texts can mitigate this increase.
